title: Erdos problem #993: a tree whose independent set sequence is not unimodal
statement: Find a tree or forest whose independent set sequence i_0, i_1, ... (i_k = the number of independent sets of k vertices) is not unimodal: it falls and later rises again. Alavi, Malde, Schwenk and Erdos (1987) asked whether this can happen. A valid counterexample scores 1.
submission: Text file: the edges of the forest, one "u v" per line with vertices numbered 0..n-1, optionally preceded by a line "n N" giving the number of vertices.
score: 1 for a counterexample; none is known, so the best known value is 0

best_known.source: no counterexample is known: T. F. Bloom, Erdos Problem #993 (erdosproblems.com/993, last edited 1 Feb 2026; status 'falsifiable' in the database teorth/erdosproblems); read 9 Nov 2026
